## Second reduction

$$\begin{matrix}
\begin{bmatrix} \text{T}_{2\text{p}} \\ \text{LT}_{2\text{p}} \end{bmatrix} & \xrightarrow{k_{\text{eff}3}(L)} & \begin{bmatrix} \text{T}_{3\text{p}} \\ \text{LT}_{3\text{p}} \end{bmatrix} \\
& \xleftarrow{k_{\text{eff}4}(L)} & \\
k_{\text{eff}1}(L) \Big\uparrow \Big\downarrow k_{\text{pt}} & & k_{\text{eff}2}(L) \Big\uparrow \Big\downarrow k_{\text{pt}} \\
\begin{bmatrix} \text{T}_2 \\ \text{LT}_2 \end{bmatrix} & \xrightarrow{k_{\text{eff}3}(L)} & \begin{bmatrix} \text{T}_3 \\ \text{LT}_3 \end{bmatrix}
\end{matrix}$$

additional assumption:
- CheB only demethylates phosphorylated receptors

experimental backup:
- not possible to directly measure if CheB demethylates only active receptors
- rate of methylation drops immediately after addition of ligand indicates that CheB works on active receptors

## Third reduction

$$\begin{matrix}
\xrightarrow{r_{\text{in}}} & \begin{bmatrix} \text{T}_{3\text{p}} \\ \text{LT}_{3\text{p}} \end{bmatrix} \\
\xleftarrow{k_{\text{eff}4}} & \\
& k_{\text{eff}2}(L) \Big\uparrow \Big\downarrow k_{\text{pt}} \\
\xrightarrow{r_{\text{in}}} & \begin{bmatrix} \text{T}_3 \\ \text{LT}_3 \end{bmatrix}
\end{matrix}$$

additional assumption:
- $[\text{CheR}] \ll [\text{receptors}]$,
  methylation operates at saturation
  ($r_{\text{in}}$ is independent of receptor concentrations)

experimental backup:
- Michaelis constant of CheR binding $\ll [\text{receptors}]$
  so $R_{\text{tot}} \sim R_{\text{bnd}}$  **ok**

## Fourth reduction

$$\begin{matrix}
\xrightarrow{r_{\text{in}}} & \begin{bmatrix} \text{T}_{3\text{p}} \\ \text{LT}_{3\text{p}} \end{bmatrix} \\
\xleftarrow{k_{\text{eff}4}} & \\
& k_{\text{eff}2}(L) \Big\uparrow \Big\downarrow k_{\text{pt}} \\
\xrightarrow{r_{\text{in}}} & \begin{bmatrix} \text{T}_3 \\ \text{LT}_3 \end{bmatrix}
\end{matrix}$$

additional assumption:
- demethylation is identical for bound and unbound receptors, so $k_{\text{eff}4}$ is independent of L.

experimental backup:
- kinetics of demethylation almost independent of level of methylation and ligand binding.  **ok**

## Refresh: Autocatalysis (Problem set #1).

$$A + X \underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_{+1}}{\rightleftharpoons}} 2X$$

$$\dot{x} = k_1 ax - k_{-1} x^2 \qquad \begin{aligned} &x = [X] \\ &a = [A] = \text{constant} \\ &\text{(e.g. enormous surplus)} \end{aligned}$$

This equation is of the type: $\dot{x} = f(x)$

first order differential equation

**Analysis recipe:**
1. determine fixed points
2. stability analysis

---

Fixed points: $f(x^*) = 0$:

$$x_1^* = 0$$
$$x_2^* = \frac{k_1 a}{k_{-1}}$$

$$k_1 a x$$
$$k_{-1} x^2$$

$$f(x) = k_1 ax - k_{-1} x^2$$

$$\dot{x} > 0$$
$$\dot{x} < 0$$

2 fixed points: one stable and one unstable

## more quantitative stability analysis:

small perturbation from fixed point:

$$\eta(t) = x(t) - x^*$$

$$f(x^* + \eta) = f(x^*) + \eta f'(x^*) + O(\eta^2) \approx \eta f'(x^*)$$

$$\dot{\eta} \approx \eta f'(x^*)$$

$$\eta(t) \sim \exp(f'(x^*)t)$$

$$f'(x^*) > 0 \qquad \text{unstable fixed point}$$
$$f'(x^*) < 0 \qquad \text{stable fixed point}$$

## Other example:

$$\begin{matrix}
\xrightarrow{r_{\text{in}}} & \begin{bmatrix} \text{T}_{3\text{p}} \\ \text{LT}_{3\text{p}} \end{bmatrix} & \mathbf{C^*} \\
\xleftarrow{k_{\text{eff}4}} & \\
& k_{\text{eff}2}(L) \Big\uparrow \Big\downarrow k_{\text{pt}} \\
\xrightarrow{r_{\text{in}}} & \begin{bmatrix} \text{T}_3 \\ \text{LT}_3 \end{bmatrix} & \mathbf{C}
\end{matrix}$$

$$\dot{C}^* = (-k_{\text{pt}} - k_{\text{eff}4})C^* + k_{\text{eff}2}C + r_{\text{in}}$$
$$\dot{C} = k_{\text{pt}}C^* - k_{\text{eff}2}C + r_{\text{in}}$$

$$\begin{aligned}
\dot{x} &= ax + by + r_{\text{in}} \\
\dot{y} &= cx + dy + r_{\text{in}}
\end{aligned} \qquad\qquad \begin{aligned}
x &\equiv C^* \\
y &\equiv C \\
a &\equiv (-k_{\text{pt}} - k_{\text{eff}4}) \\
b &\equiv k_{\text{eff}2} \\
c &\equiv k_{\text{pt}} \\
d &\equiv -b
\end{aligned}$$
